# Page 24^page=24
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 24 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Overview of PM Narendra Modi’s Visit to Gujarat on March 31, 2026 On March 31 2026, Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi visited Gujarat where he visited Gandhinagar, Sanand (Ahmedabad) and Vav–Tharad (Banaskantha) to launch and dedicate multiple development projects worth over Rs. 20,000 crore. Exam Hints: ✓ What? PM Narendra Modi’s visited Gujarat ✓ Where? Gandhinagar, Sanand (Ahmedabad), Vav–Tharad (Banaskantha region) ✓ Gandhinagar: Samrat Samprati Museum inaugurated at Koba Tirth ✓ Sanand: Inauguration of Kaynes Semicon Plant (GIDC Sanand) ✓ Vav–Tharad: Inaugurated projects worth More than Rs. 20,000 crore across Power, Railways, Roads, Urban, Health, Tourism, Water, Tribal development. Visit to Gandhinagar: Inauguration: On the occasion of Mahavir Jayanti, the PM Narendra Modi inaugurated the Samrat Samprati Museum at Koba Tirth in Gandhinagar(Gujarat), dedicated to showcasing the rich historical, cultural, and spiritual legacy of Jainism. Legacy: Named after Samrat Samprati, grandson of Ashoka and a revered figure in Jain tradition, the museum highlights his contributions to non-violence and the propagation of Jainism. Location: Situated within the Mahavir Jain Aradhana Kendra campus, the museum presents a comprehensive journey through India’s civilizational heritage. Galleries: The museum comprises seven distinct galleries featuring over 2,000 rare artefacts, including ancient manuscripts, stone and metal idols, miniature paintings, coins, silver chariots, and traditional Jain relics. Technology: It integrates traditional displays with modern digital and audio-visual installations to create an immersive and engaging experience for visitors, researchers, and scholars. Visit to Sanand: Inauguration: PM Narendra Modi inaugurated the Kaynes Semicon Plant at Sanand , Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC), Ahmedabad, marking the commencement of commercial semiconductor production in India. Production: The facility began manufacturing advanced Intelligent Power Modules (IPMs) for automotive and industrial applications, with each module comprising 17 chips supplied to California-based Alpha and Omega Semiconductor (AOS). Capacity: Upon full completion, the plant is projected to produce 6.33 million units per day (MUPD), significantly enhancing India’s semiconductor manufacturing scale. Mission: The project represents a major milestone under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), becoming the second facility after Micron Technology to commence commercial production. Facility: Established as an OSAT/ATMP (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test / Assembly, Testing, Marking, and Packaging) unit, it marks the entry of an Indian-origin Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) player into semiconductor manufacturing. Visit to Vav-Tharad: Overview: During his visit to Gujarat, he laid the foundation stone, inaugurated, and dedicated to the nation multiple development projects worth over Rs. 20,000 crore across key

Railways: He dedicated and inaugurated multiple rail projects including the Kanalus–Jamnagar doubling project (28 kilometer, km), Gandhidham–Adipur quadrupling (10.69 km), and Himmatnagar–Khedbrahma gauge conversion (54.83 km), and flagged off the Khedbrahma–Himmatnagar–Asarwa train to enhance rail capacity and connectivity. Urban: He inaugurated and laid the foundation stone of 44 urban development projects worth around Rs. 5,300 crore, along with Sabarmati Riverfront expansion works, to improve urban infrastructure and quality of life. Health: He inaugurated health and welfare initiatives including 858-bed Rain Basera facilities at Civil Hospital, Asarwa and at Gandhinagar Civil Hospital and GMERS Medical College to strengthen public healthcare support. Tourism: He inaugurated tourism projects such as the Light and Sound Show at Rani ki Vav and Water Screen Projection at Sharmishtha Lake, and laid the foundation for tourism infrastructure at Balaram Mahadev and Vishweshwar Mahadev. Water: dedicated two major water pipeline projects worth around Rs. 1,780 crore, including the Kasara– Dantiwada Pipeline in Banaskantha and the Dindrol–Mukteshwar Pipeline across Patan and Banaskantha. • He also laid the foundation stone for a water supply scheme benefiting Ambaji and 34 nearby villages covering about 1.5 lakh people, along with three Sabarmati Riverfront expansion projects in Gandhinagar district worth around Rs. 1,000 crore. Tribal: He inaugurated the Government Boys Hostel at Vejalpur, Ahmedabad, to support tribal students pursuing higher education. About Gujarat: Chief Minister (CM)– Bhupendrabhai Patel Governor- Acharya Devvrat Capital- Gandhinagar National Park (NP)- Thol Lake Wildlife Sanctuary Nalsarovar Bird Sanctuary GoI Extends National Piped Natural Gas Drive 2.0 Till June 30, 2026 In March 2026, the Government of India (GoI) extended the National Piped Natural Gas (PNG) Drive 2.0 by three months till 30 June 2026 to sustain momentum in nationwide PNG expansion and increase the share of natural gas to 15% in India’s energy basket. • The initiative, earlier scheduled to end on 31 March 2026, has been extended to accelerate PNG connectivity and strengthen the transition towards a gas-based economy. Exam Hints: ✓ What? National PNG Drive 2.0 extended ✓ When? Till 30 June 2026 (from 31 March 2026) ✓ Why? Boost PNG connectivity & achieve 15% gas share

About National PNG Drive 2.0: Background: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) launched the National PNG Drive from 26 January 2024 to 31 March 2024. • The campaign, in collaboration with City Gas Distribution (CGD) companies, aims to promote widespread adoption of domestic PNG and expand its consumer base. PNG Drive 2.0 Launch: The PNGRB launched PNG Drive 2.0 from 1 January 2026 to 31 March 2026, bringing together City Gas Distribution (CGD) companies under the theme “Har Ghar PNG, Har Gaadi CNG.” Targeted Expansion: Under the initiative, the government aims to extend natural gas pipeline connectivity to 37 additional Geographical Areas (GAs) not connected to the national gas pipeline and 44 districts without PNG network access. Current Progress: In March 2026 alone, India added over 310,000 new connections and issued another 270,000 connections for domestic and commercial users. New Legislation: The government notified the Natural Gas and Petroleum Products Distribution Order, 2026, under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, to streamline land access and address pipeline construction delays. Incentives for PNG Adoption: CGD companies are offering incentives such as free gas worth Rs. 500, waiver of registration charges, and removal of security deposits to promote PNG connections. About Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG): Union Minister – Hardeep Singh Puri (Rajya Sabha- Uttar Pradesh, UP) Minister of State (MoS) – Suresh Gopi (Constituency – Thrissur, Kerala) VP CP Radhakrishnan Unveils ‘Nyaya Setu’ AI Chatbot and Mascot ‘Dishika’ at DISHA Programme in New Delhi In March 2026, Vice-President Chandrapuram Ponnusami (C.P.) # Page 27^page=27
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 27 Daily Content PDF ✓ Nyaya Setu: AI-powered legal assistant (voice-first, multilingual) ✓ Developed by: DIBD, MeitY ✓ Tech Used: ASR + NLP + Conversational AI ✓ Alignment: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ✓ Mascot: Dishika – guides users in legal queries. About Nyaya Setu AI Chatbot: Overview: Nyaya Setu is a voice-first, multimodal, multilingual Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered legal assistant designed to help citizens understand legal processes, rights, and next steps through simple voice and text interactions in multiple Indian languages. Objective: It aims to democratise access to justice, particularly for individuals facing linguistic and procedural barriers. Developing Authority: The platform has been developed by the Digital India BHASHINI(BHASHA INterface for India) Division (DIBD) under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). Technology: It is built on a complete end-to-end voice stack, integrating Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and conversational AI systems. Alignment: It is aligned with legal frameworks such as the ‘Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)’ to ensure safe and context-aware responses. About Mascot: Role: ‘Dishika’ serves as a friendly digital interface that guides users through legal queries. Significance: It enhances accessibility, trust, and user engagement, especially for first-time users navigating the justice system. About BHASHINI: Overview: BHASHINI is India’s AI-powered language technology initiative under the MeitY, implemented by the DIBD under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), a Section 8 company. Developer: It has developed the National Hub for Language Technology (NHLT), one of the world’s largest AI inferencing platforms, enabling multilingual capabilities across Indian and international languages through advanced speech and text technologies. Key Features: It supports 500+ government websites and processes over 15 million inferences daily. • It provides 20+ specialised Natural Language Processing (NLP) services across 36 text and 23 voice languages, including support for tribal dialects and multiple international languages, while fostering an ecosystem of open-source AI models. About DISHA Scheme: Overview: Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice (DISHA) is a Central Sector Scheme (CSS) implemented by the Department of Justice (DoJ), MoL&J. • It was launched in 2021 with an outlay of Rs. 250 crore for 2021–2026. Objective: It aims to provide integrated access to justice across India through Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu, and Legal Awareness programmes. Key Features: The scheme is citizen-centric and technology-driven. Under Tele-Law, free pre-litigation legal advice is provided via Common Service Centres (CSCs), mobile application(apps), and toll-free number 14454. • It is operational in over 2.5 lakh CSCs across 776 districts in 36 States/Union Territories (UTs), including 112 Aspirational Districts and 500 Aspirational Blocks. About Ministry of Law& Justice (MoL&J): Union Minister of State (MoS) (Independent Charge, IC)– Arjun Ram Meghwal (Constituency- Bikaner, Rajasthan)

Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 28 Daily Content PDF INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS Overview of WTO’s 14th Ministerial Conference Held in Yaoundé, Cameroon In March 2026, the World Trade Organization (WTO) held its 14th Ministerial Conference (MC14) from March 26 to 30, 2026 in Yaoundé, Cameroon, focusing on key challenges and future priorities of the global multilateral trading system. • The conference was chaired by Luc Magloire Mbarga Atangana, Minister of Trade of Cameroon. Exam Hints: ✓ What? 14th Ministerial Conference (MC14) of WTO held ✓ Where? Yaoundé, Cameroon ✓ Chair: Luc Magloire Mbarga Atangana, Minister of Trade of Cameroon ✓ India Led by: Piyush Goyal (MoC&I) ✓ Key Outcomes: ✓ Fisheries subsidies talks to continue till MC15 ✓ Decisions on small economies integration & S&DT ✓ Yaoundé Package. Highlights of WTO’s MC14: Overview: The Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body of the WTO and is usually held once every two years (biennial). • The 2026 meeting marked the second WTO Ministerial Conference to be held in Africa. Participation: Around 2,000 trade officials, including more than 90 ministers, participated in the conference. About India’s Participation: Indian Delegation: The Indian team was led by Union Minister Piyush Goyal, Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I), supported by officials from the Permanent Mission of India in Geneva, Switzerland. India’s Stand at MC14: India emphasised the need for an open, fair, inclusive, and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system, with the WTO at the core of global trade governance. • It also highlighted key priorities, including a permanent solution on Public Stockholding (PSH) for food security, strengthening of Special and Differential Treatment (S&DT) provisions for developing and Least Developed Countries (LDCs), and the restoration of a fully functional dispute settlement mechanism. Outcomes of MC14: Fisheries Subsidies: Members agreed to continue negotiations with the goal of finalizing comprehensive disciplines by the 15th Ministerial Conference (MC15). Integration of Economies: Two significant decisions were adopted to better integrate small economies and enhance the implementation of S&DT in Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) and Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) agreements. Yaoundé Package: While a full final agreement was not reached, a “Yaoundé Package” was developed to serve as a basis for finalization in Geneva, Switzerland. • This includes the Draft Ministerial Declaration on WTO Reform, the Decision on Electronic Commerce (Work Programme and Moratorium), and the Moratorium on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) Non-Violation and Situation Complaints. • Discussions on pending issues will continue in Geneva, Switzerland, during upcoming WTO meetings.
